question: Which article of Indian Constitution talks about Advocate-General for the State?
solution:
The correct answer is __**165**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 165** of the Indian Constitution is related to the office of **Advocate General of State**.

 
 
• He is the** highest law officer of the state.**
 
 
 
• The appointment of the Advocate General is done by the Governor on the advice of the council of ministers of the state.
 
• The person who is eligible to hold the office of advocate general in India must meet the following criteria:
 
 
• He must be an **Indian Citizen.**
 
• He should be **eligible to be appointed as the judge of the High Court**; i.e. he must meet one of the following eligibility criteria:
 
 
• A barrister having experience of more than 5 years.
 
• A civil servant with an experience of more than 10 years along with an experience as a servant in Zila Court for at least 3 years.
 
• A pleader over 10 years in any high court
 
 
 
• He **shouldn’t be more than 62 years of age**, as is the age qualification for a High Court Judge.
 
 
 
• The Constitution **does not fix the term** of Advocate General in India. He remains in the office during the pleasure of the Governor.
 
• The process and justifications for removing the Advocate General of State are not found in the Constitution. The **governor has the right to remove him or her at any time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Duties and functions** of the **Advocate General of State**:

 
 
• When the governor directs him to counsel on legal concerns, it is his duty to advise the state government.
 
• In addition, he must carry out any legal responsibilities delegated to him by the state governor.
 
• He is obligated by the Constitution to carry out the tasks and responsibilities specified in it or in any other constitutional law.
 
 
 
• **Article 145** of Indian Constitution deals with the **Rules of Courts,** etc.
 
• **Article 77** of Indian Constitution mentions the **Conduct of business of the Government of India**.
 
• **Article 136** of Indian Constitution addresses the **special leave to appeal by the Supreme court**.
 
 
• It means that, with the exception of military tribunals and court-martials, the Supreme Court is empowered to grant, at its discretion, special leave to appeal from any judgment in any case rendered by any court or tribunal within the borders of India.
 
 
 
• Attorney General of India:
 
 
• Article 76 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, duties, and qualifications of the Attorney General of India.
 
 
• The Attorney General of India will be appointed by the President from among those who meet the requirements to be appointed as Supreme Court judges.
 
• The Attorney General will serve as long as the President so desires.
 
 
 
• He is the chief law officer in the country.
 
 
• He provides legal advice to the Government of India and represents the Government in legal matters.
 
• He also has the power to appear in any court of law in India and can take part in any proceedings that affect the Government of India.
 
• Thus he have the right of audience in all Indian courts while carrying out his duties.
 
 
 
• Under Article 88 of the Indian Constitution, he is free to participate in and speak at any session of the Houses of Parliament, as well as in any joint session, and to be appointed to any committee of the Parliament; however, he is not entitled to vote. 
 
• He is entitled to all the privileges and immunities that are granted to members of Parliament.
